hints: Focus on what each chemical test is really telling you about the functional groups present in X.
Remember that 2,4-DNPH gives an orange precipitate only with aldehydes and ketones, while warmed acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-$ is decolourised by alkenes and aldehydes but not by ketones.
Check which structure contains an aldehyde group for both tests to be positive and also simplifies to the empirical formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{O}$.
walkthrough:
**Decode the two chemical tests**

Great start, let's translate the observations into functional groups. A positive 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine test means a carbonyl group, so X must be an aldehyde or a ketone.

Test rule:
$$\text{aldehyde or ketone} \rightarrow \text{orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH}$$

**Use the manganate(VII) result to narrow it down**

Warmed acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ is purple and is decolourised when it oxidises something. Alkenes and aldehydes do this, but ketones are resistant to oxidation and do not.

So to pass both tests, X most simply needs an aldehyde group:
$$\text{RCHO} + [\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{RCOOH}, \text{ purple } \text{MnO}_4^- \rightarrow \text{colourless } \text{Mn}^{2+}$$

**Check the empirical formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{O}$**

Now count atoms for the aldehyde candidate. Option A is $\text{OHCCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, which is butanedial.

Molecular formula:
$$\text{C}_4\text{H}_6\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{divide by 2} \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{O}$$
This matches perfectly, has two aldehyde groups for a positive DNPH test, and aldehydes are oxidised so it decolourises $\text{KMnO}_4$.

options.A: Correct. This is $\text{OHC-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CHO}$ (butanedial). Molecular formula is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$ which simplifies to $\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{O}$. The aldehyde groups give an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH and are easily oxidised to carboxylic acids, so warmed acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ is decolourised.
options.B: False. This is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCOCH}_3$ (butane-2,3-dione). Although its formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$ gives the correct empirical formula and its ketone groups give a positive DNPH test, ketones resist oxidation and will not decolourise warmed acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$.
options.C: False. This is $\text{CH}_2\text{=C(CH}_3\text{)COOH}$ (2-methylpropenoic acid). Its formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$ fits the empirical formula and its C=C bond decolourises $\text{KMnO}_4$, but a carboxylic acid is not an aldehyde or ketone so it gives no orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH.
options.D: False. This is $\text{HOOC(CH}_2\text{)}_4\text{CHO}$ (5-formylpentanoic acid). It would give both chemical tests because it has an aldehyde, but its molecular formula is $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_3$ which does not simplify to $\text{C}_2\text{H}_3\text{O}$. Students choosing this spot the functional groups but forget to check the empirical formula.
